info.bio:
The Spencer Davis Group es un grupo dentro de la avalancha que se ha dado en llamar "British Invasion" en los años sesenta.
En él sobresale la figura de un jovencísimo Stevie Winwood, cantante y organista, que luego pasaría por grupos como 'Blind Faith' -con Ginger Baker y Eric Clapton (ex Cream's) y Rich Grech- y 'Traffic' -Ginger Baker, Jim Capaldi et alli-.
Entre los mayores éxitos de Spencer Davis Group se encuentran 'Gimme Some Lovin' y I'm A Man (de la que luego haría una sensacional versión el Grupo Chicago (Transit Authority)

scenes.name: Beat, R&B y mod pop británico
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Tras el éxito de los Beatles, las cuatro grandes discográficas (EMI, Decca, Pye y Philips) saquearon metódicamente las provincias: firmaban barato y esperaban a ver qué pegaba. Pye, del veterano Louis Benjamin, tenía a los Kinks y a los Searchers y fama de contratos miserables. Los Ugly’s de Birmingham, nacidos del skiffle y curtidos en los clubes alemanes, se distinguían por su conciencia social; la cara B de su tercer single, «A Quiet Explosion» (21 de enero de 1966), con órgano Vox Continental, un riff con eco a lo Delia Derbyshire y un bajo descendente que es la bomba cayendo, desapareció en la sobreproducción del momento, pero es un disco extraño y auténtico que se acerca a la psicodelia. A principios de 1966 las bases del beat y del R&B se llevaron al límite, como bajo una enorme presión: «Keep on Running» de Spencer Davis casa soul y mod pop, los Wheels de Belfast aceleran sin freno en «Bad Little Woman» y los Poets de Glasgow, de Andrew Loog Oldham, desquician el «Baby Don’t You Do It» de Marvin Gaye.

scenes.name: Rock progresivo
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Al emigrar a Gran Bretaña, el rock se convierte en mercancía de moda pero también se descontextualiza: lo que en EE UU era el diario de la juventud se vuelve en Gran Bretaña un ensayo. El progresivo no comenta la cultura juvenil sino que busca la innovación técnica: arranca con las óperas rock (S.F. Sorrow, Tommy) y los álbumes conceptuales, lo cimentan Traffic, Jeff Beck, Jethro Tull, Family y Genesis, y alcanza su cima con King Crimson (In The Court Of The Crimson King), Van Der Graaf Generator y Yes. Colosseum, la Third Ear Band (inventores de la world music), las variantes góticas (High Tide, Black Widow) y folk (Comus, Strawbs), Gentle Giant, Emerson Lake & Palmer y Roxy Music, que revoluciona el género y prepara la new wave y el synth-pop.

podcast.title: Collaboration with Millie Small
podcast.body: The group was teamed with Millie Small in an attempt to replicate her earlier success, but this collaboration did not lead to a resurgence in her chart performance. "the Spencer Davis group didn't revive her fortunes."

podcast.title: Discovery by Chris Blackwell
podcast.body: This rock group was discovered by Chris Blackwell, who foresaw their future as big stars. They gained significant popularity by performing versions of songs written by Jackie Edwards. "the rock group Blackwell had discovered, and who would soon become big stars themselves with versions of songs by Edwards."

xref.title: Dog's Lottery Jackpot (2012)
xref.body: Spencer Davis, the figure behind The Spencer Davis Group, had a unique system for playing the lottery weekly, using three sets of numbers: one for himself, one for his wife, and one for his dog. In 2012, it was the dog's set of numbers that won a substantial jackpot of $250,000. "In 2012, the dog hit a jackpot of $250,000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Father's Discouragement and Early Bands
xref.body: His father, Ringo Starr, gave him only one drum lesson and attempted to discourage him from a career in show business, advising him to be a doctor or lawyer instead of a musician. Despite this, Zach first joined a garage band called The Next, then a reformed version of the Spencer Davis Group. "Dad gave him exactly one lesson before he tried to dissuade his son about getting into show business. Be a doctor, be a lawyer, don't be a musician. Yeah, that didn't work. First came a garage band called The Next. Then he ended up in a reformed version of the Spencer Davis group."
